title: Seawall Rules in Broward County
question: What are the seawall requirements in Broward County?
unit: ft NAVD88 minimum (4.0 if applied for before 2035)
qualifier: Broward is the one county in South Florida with a single standard behind every city, and the number most people quote is the wrong one. The minimum is 5 ft NAVD88. The 4 ft figure you will hear is an allowance: an application filed before 1 January 2035 may be permitted at 4 ft, if the barrier is built to reach 5 ft by 1 January 2050. It is not a floor you are entitled to, and cities answer it differently, so the number that applies to you is your city's.
detail_rows: The standard :: Tidal flood barriers must have a minimum elevation of 5 ft NAVD88. Broward County Code Sec. 39-407(a). | The 2035 allowance :: Applications for new or substantially repaired barriers submitted before 1 January 2035 may be permitted at 4 ft NAVD88, if designed and constructed to accommodate 5 ft NAVD88 by 1 January 2050. Sec. 39-407(a). | It is not a right :: The code says such applications may be permitted, and Article XXV defines may as permissive. Budget for 5 ft and treat 4 ft as the exception you have to ask for. Secs. 39-406, 39-407(a). | Where it comes from :: Broward County Code Chapter 39, Article XXV, Resiliency Standards for Tidal Flood Protection, Secs. 39-404 to 39-408, adopted by Ord. No. 2020-11 on 31 March 2020. Sec. 39-407 sets the elevations; Sec. 39-404 is the purpose statement. Broward County Land Use Plan Policy 2.21.7 sits behind it. | Every city had to adopt it :: The county's own guidance says local governments were required to adopt an implementing ordinance by 13 February 2022. | Fort Lauderdale :: 5.0 ft NAVD88 minimum with the same pre-2035 4 ft route, and a cap: the base flood elevation or 6.0 ft NAVD88, whichever is lower. ULDR 47-19.13.D(1), D(12). | Hollywood :: 5 ft NAVD88 minimum with the same pre-2035 4 ft route, plus at least one cubic yard per linear foot of riprap or approved habitat enhancement, and a review of the standard due by 2034. Code Sec. 150.30. | Pompano Beach :: 5 ft NAVD88 minimum and 5 ft 10 in maximum, with no pre-2035 4 ft route in its text. Code § 151.05(A). | Not the only cap :: Several Broward cities set a maximum as well as a minimum: Pompano Beach, Fort Lauderdale, Deerfield Beach (7 ft NAVD88 or the required finished grade, whichever is higher, LDC 98-87(d)(4)b) and Hillsboro Beach (the property's base flood elevation, Code Sec. 12-268(D)). | Selling a waterfront home :: Sale contracts for property in tidally influenced areas executed after 31 December 2020 must carry the county disclosure in capitalised bold type of at least 14 point. Sec. 39-408. | The practical point :: Build to 4 ft today and the wall has to come up again before 2050. Ask what it costs to build to 5 ft now, while the barge is already there.
source: Broward County Code Ch. 39, Art. XXV, Secs. 39-404 to 39-408 (Ord. No. 2020-11, 3-31-20; Municode Supp. 72); Broward County "Build It High, Keep It Dry" regional standard guidance (adoption deadline); City of Hollywood Code Sec. 150.30 (Ord. O-2022-01); Fort Lauderdale ULDR Sec. 47-19.13; Pompano Beach Code § 151.05; Deerfield Beach LDC Sec. 98-87(d)(4)b; Hillsboro Beach Code Sec. 12-268

title: Seawall Rules in Miami-Dade County
question: What are the seawall requirements in Miami-Dade County?
unit: the number is set by your city
qualifier: Miami-Dade works the opposite way to Broward. The county runs the environmental permit through Chapter 24, but it sets no countywide seawall elevation — that is your city's decision, and the cities differ sharply. What the county does control is how far waterward you may rebuild, and that single measurement decides which permit route you are on.
detail_rows: The county's part :: Chapter 24 environmental permitting through DERM, which applies inside every city in the county. | The 18-inch rule :: A seawall rebuilt at the mean high water line or up to 18 inches waterward of its existing line (or up to 18 inches beyond existing support piles that stick out no more than 14 inches) qualifies for a short-form permit decided by DERM. Seawall-only work cannot be pulled into a County Commission hearing. Since Ord. 25-73 (July 2025), standard-form applications are also decided by the DERM Director, except for variances that require a hearing or substantial changes to a Commission-approved permit or covenant. | Why that matters :: Beyond 18 inches, the county's delegated state and federal authority may not apply, so separate state (FDEP) and Army Corps approval may be needed (Ord. 25-73 recitals). For short-form seawall permits the county targets a completeness review within 10 days and a decision within 90 days after it (Ord. 25-73 Sec. 8, from 1 Dec 2025). | Where it is written :: Miami-Dade County Code Section 24-48.2, as amended by Ord. 25-73 (7-1-25). | Elevation is municipal :: The county sets no height. Miami Beach requires 5.7 ft NAVD88. Other cities set their own, and several have not published one at all. | Miami Beach specifically :: 5.7 ft NAVD88 for new or substantially improved walls, with an interim 4.0 ft allowed for lesser repairs if the wall is built to accept 5.7 ft later. Substantial now means repairs of $500 or more per linear foot, raised from $300 in July 2025. | Budget for a bond :: Some cities in the county require a refundable bond on top of the contract. Confirm the current amount with the city - it is not in the contractor's bid. Ask before you sign.
source: Miami-Dade County Code Sec. 24-48.2 (as amended by Ord. 25-73, 7-1-25); City of Miami Beach Code Sec. 54-62(a), Ordinance 2025-4754

title: Seawall Rules in Palm Beach County
question: What are the seawall requirements in Palm Beach County?
qualifier: Palm Beach is the hardest of the four counties to get a straight answer in. Broward has one standard every city adopted; Palm Beach does not work that way. Some towns set an elevation in their own document, many set none at all, and two neighbouring towns can differ. The rule is also not always in the code where you would look for it first.
detail_rows: How this county differs :: Broward's towns all adopted one county standard. Of the Palm Beach County towns we have verified, Boca Raton, Delray Beach, North Palm Beach (Sec. 5-72), Tequesta (Sec. 76-33) and Ocean Ridge (Sec. 64-82) set a seawall elevation, each in its own code. Jupiter, West Palm Beach, Boynton Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, Juno Beach, Riviera Beach, Lantana, Lake Worth Beach, South Palm Beach and Manalapan set none, and Gulf Stream sets only a maximum of 8 ft NGVD (Sec. 70-78). | Boca Raton :: 4.0 ft NAVD88 minimum, 6.0 ft maximum. The wall must also be built so a further 12 to 18 inches can be added later without altering it. | Two documents in Boca :: The 4.0 to 6.0 ft NAVD88 band is in the Engineering Design Standards Manual, section 7.7. The Code of Ordinances separately says no bulkhead may be built lower than plus 5.00 feet, with no datum stated (Sec. 22-31(5)). Ask the city in writing which it applies. | Delray Beach :: 4.2 ft NAVD88 minimum in every flood zone, for new seawalls, substantial repairs and fixed structures attached to them (LDR 7.1.7(B)). The maximum varies with your FEMA flood zone — your base flood elevation where that is 5.0 ft or higher, 5 ft where the BFE is 4.0. | Delray's extra obligation :: Any contract to sell property in a tidally influenced area of Delray Beach, signed after 1 February 2022, must carry a tidal flood barrier disclosure in bold capitals of at least 14 point. The duty attaches to the sale contract (LDR 7.1.7(D)(7)). | Build low, engineer high :: Both towns require a wall built under the higher figure to be designed so it can be raised later. Building to the minimum today does not close the question. | What to ask your town :: What is the minimum cap elevation, in which datum, and where is it written — the code, or an engineering standards manual? The second half of that question is the one that saves you a week.
source: City of Boca Raton Engineering Design Standards Manual § 7.7 and Code of Ordinances Ch. 22, Sec. 22-31(5); City of Delray Beach Land Development Regulations Sec. 7.1.7 and Table 7.1.7(D), Ordinance 23-21; North Palm Beach Code Sec. 5-72; Tequesta Code Sec. 76-33; Ocean Ridge Code Sec. 64-82; Gulf Stream Code Sec. 70-78

title: Seawall Rules in Monroe County and the Florida Keys
question: What are the seawall requirements in Monroe County?
qualifier: Monroe is the only county of the four where we can say with certainty that no elevation standard exists, because we read every mention of seawall and bulkhead in the county's code to establish it. That does not make the Keys permissive. Monroe regulates something the other three counties largely do not - whether you may build a vertical wall at all.
detail_rows: No minimum, no maximum :: Monroe County Land Development Code Sec. 118-12(k) sets no elevation and no datum for a seawall or bulkhead. Every seawall and bulkhead reference in the Code of Ordinances, the Land Development Code and the Comprehensive Plan was checked. | The real restriction is location :: A vertical seawall or bulkhead is permitted only to stabilise a severely eroding shoreline, and only on manmade canals, channels or basins. Sec. 118-12(k)(3). | It is a last resort :: Permitted only if native vegetation, or riprap and filter cloth, is not a feasible means to control erosion. Sec. 118-12(k)(3). | Open water is closed :: No new seawalls, bulkheads or other hardened vertical structures are permitted on open water. Comprehensive Plan Policy 210.1.6 goes further - seawalls are prohibited on any beach or open-water shoreline. | Repair is protected :: A lawfully existing deteriorated seawall may be repaired or replaced, and is exempt from the nonsubstantial-improvements limit, except on known or potential sea turtle nesting beaches. The work must keep the existing footprint to the maximum extent practicable. Sec. 118-12(k)(4). | Turtles outrank the wall :: No seawall, bulkhead or riprap on or waterward of a beach berm complex that is known or potential marine turtle nesting area, as determined by the County Biologist. Sec. 118-12(k)(7). | Riprap and mangroves :: Riprap at the toe wherever feasible, and barriers placed landward of existing mangroves whenever feasible. Sec. 118-12(k)(5) and (6). | The one height-adjacent rule :: Existing grade landward of the bulkhead must be at least six inches lower than the top of the bulkhead. Sec. 118-12(k)(2). That fixes grade against the cap. It does not tell you how high the cap must be. | A wall with no house :: A seawall without a principal use may have a cap no more than two feet wide. Sec. 118-12(k)(1). | State and federal come first :: All such projects require state and/or federal permits before construction and before the county issues a Notice to Proceed. Sec. 118-12(k)(9). A separate county permit is required for a seawall. Code of Ordinances Sec. 6-100(b). | One city does set a height :: Key Colony Beach requires 5.5 ft above mean sea level (Code Sec. 5-51). Of the other Keys codes we have read, none sets one: Key West (Sec. 110-182), Marathon (LDR Sec. 106.36(H)), Islamorada (Village Code Sec. 30-1545) and unincorporated Monroe (LDC Sec. 118-12(k)). We have not yet read Layton's code.
source: Monroe County Land Development Code Sec. 118-12(k), Shoreline Setbacks; Monroe County Comprehensive Plan Policies 210.1.6 and 212.5.1-212.5.4; Monroe County Code of Ordinances Sec. 6-100(b); Key Colony Beach Code Sec. 5-51; Key West Code Sec. 110-182; Marathon LDR Sec. 106.36(H); Islamorada Village Code Sec. 30-1545
